METADATA.title: How To Tell If Your Vintage Guitar Has Been Refinished
METADATA.description: Learn where to look for a guitar refinish, from the headstock and hardware to finish wear. I'll explain the clues and what needs a bench inspection.
METADATA.h1: How To Tell If A Vintage Guitar Has Been Refinished
METADATA.primaryQuery: how to tell if a guitar has been refinished

mainEntity.name: Does A Shiny Old Guitar Have To Be Refinished?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Some original finishes remain bright and smooth. Shine, checking or yellowing alone cannot establish originality; the materials, wear and construction need to agree.

mainEntity.name: Can A Blacklight Prove A Finish Is Original?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Ultraviolet response is supporting evidence. Different materials and aging can produce different responses, and an old repaint can still look convincing.

mainEntity.name: Should I Remove The Neck Or Pickguard To Check?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Send photographs of what is already visible and keep any existing inspection photographs. Leave disassembly to a specialist who can decide what needs to be examined.

mainEntity.name: Is A Fender Decal Buried Under Lacquer A Warning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. On the vintage Fender headstocks discussed here, the water-slide decal was applied last, over the clear coat. A decal buried beneath lacquer means the headstock was resprayed.

mainEntity.name: Can Fender Factory Work Be A Refinish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fender operated a repair and refinish service. Later factory work can resemble production finish closely, so repair-department evidence and the instrument's history need to be considered.
